HIGH dom_xss screenshot DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting (DOM XSS) in 'query'
Click to view details ▾
Vulnerable Endpoint
GET http://demo.testfire.net/search.jsp?query=<script>document.body.style.backgroundColor='red';document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin','<h1>dastXSS</h1>')</script> • Param: query
Vulnerability Description
Parameter or URL fragment flows into an unsafe client-side DOM sink without sanitization.
Technical Evidence:
Live DOM XSS confirmed in browser. Injected vector executed in client-side DOM sink. Target URL: http://demo.testfire.net/search.jsp?query=<script>document.body.style.backgroundColor='red';document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin','<h1>dastXSS</h1>')</script> Payload: <script>document.body.style.backgroundColor='red';document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin','<h1>dastXSS</h1>')</script>
📸 Visual Screenshot Evidence:
Path: C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\SCANNER\evidence\screenshots\dom_xss\step_004_dom_xss_query_evidence_279b72.png (Click image to view full resolution)
Recommended Remediation
Avoid passing untrusted URL parameters or location hashes to innerHTML/document.write. Use textContent or DOMPurify.

HIGH csrf screenshot Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) via Sensitive GET Form
Click to view details ▾
Vulnerable Endpoint
GET http://demo.testfire.net/bank/showAccount
Vulnerability Description
The form uses HTTP GET to perform sensitive state-changing operations without including a synchronized anti-CSRF token. Using HTTP GET for sensitive state modification allows trivial one-click/zero-click exploitation via hyperlinks, <img>, or <iframe> tags without user awareness.
Technical Evidence:
DOM Form Evidence: Form Method: GET Form Action: showAccount Input Fields: listAccounts Form HTML Snippet: <form action="showAccount" method="get" name="details"> <table border="0"> <tr valign="top"> <td>View Account Details:</td> <td align="left"> <select id="listAccounts" name="listAccounts" size="1"> <option value="800002">800002 Savings</option> <option value="800003">800003 Checking</option> <option value="4539082039396288">4539082039396288 Credit ... Observed: No hidden anti-CSRF token input field detected inside form.

Recommended Remediation
1. Convert sensitive state-changing actions from HTTP GET to HTTP POST. 2. Include cryptographically random, unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens in all state-changing HTML forms. 3. Enforce 'SameSite=Lax' or 'SameSite=Strict' on session cookies. 4. Require re-authentication (current password) for critical account actions (e.g., password change, email change).

HIGH csrf screenshot Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) via Sensitive GET Form

Vulnerable Endpoint
GET http://demo.testfire.net/bank/main.jsp
Vulnerability Description
The form uses HTTP GET to perform sensitive state-changing operations without including a synchronized anti-CSRF token. Using HTTP GET for sensitive state modification allows trivial one-click/zero-click exploitation via hyperlinks, <img>, or <iframe> tags without user awareness.
Technical Evidence:
DOM Form Evidence: Form Method: GET Form Action: showAccount Input Fields: listAccounts Form HTML Snippet: <form action="showAccount" method="get" name="details"> <table border="0"> <tr valign="top"> <td>View Account Details:</td> <td align="left"> <select id="listAccounts" name="listAccounts" size="1"> <option value="800002">800002 Savings</option> <option value="800003">800003 Checking</option> <option value="4539082039396288">4539082039396288 Credit ... Observed: No hidden anti-CSRF token input field detected inside form.

Recommended Remediation
1. Convert sensitive state-changing actions from HTTP GET to HTTP POST. 2. Include cryptographically random, unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens in all state-changing HTML forms. 3. Enforce 'SameSite=Lax' or 'SameSite=Strict' on session cookies. 4. Require re-authentication (current password) for critical account actions (e.g., password change, email change).

HIGH xss screenshot Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Form Field 'query'
Click to view details ▾
Vulnerable Endpoint
GET http://demo.testfire.net/search.jsp • Param: query
Vulnerability Description
Form field 'query' is vulnerable to reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
Technical Evidence:
Visual XSS confirmed. Injected payload '<script>document.body.style.backgroundColor='red';document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin','<h1>dastXSS</h1>')</script>' executed in DOM with visual indicators.
📸 Visual Screenshot Evidence:
Path: C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\SCANNER\evidence\screenshots\xss\step_011_xss_query_evidence_f1f64e.png (Click image to view full resolution)
Recommended Remediation
Contextually encode all user-supplied output (e.g. HTML entity encoding) and enforce a strict CSP.

HIGH xss screenshot Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Form Field 'query'
Click to view details ▾
Vulnerable Endpoint
GET http://demo.testfire.net/search.jsp • Param: query
Vulnerability Description
Form field 'query' is vulnerable to reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
Technical Evidence:
Visual XSS confirmed. Injected payload '<script>document.body.style.backgroundColor='red';document.body.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin','<h1>dastXSS</h1>')</script>' executed in DOM with visual indicators.
📸 Visual Screenshot Evidence:
Path: C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\SCANNER\evidence\screenshots\xss\step_012_xss_query_evidence_0ac6f8.png (Click image to view full resolution)
Recommended Remediation
Contextually encode all user-supplied output (e.g. HTML entity encoding) and enforce a strict CSP.

Contextually encode all user-supplied output (e.g. HTML entity encoding) and enforce a strict CSP.

Recommended Remediation
1. Convert sensitive state-changing actions from HTTP GET to HTTP POST. 2. Include cryptographically random, unpredictable anti-CSRF tokens in all state-changing HTML forms. 3. Enforce 'SameSite=Lax' or 'SameSite=Strict' on session cookies. 4. Require re-authentication (current password) for critical account actions (e.g., password change, email change).
